Two pointers keeps two positions in one sequence and moves them by a rule, so one pass does the work a nested loop would otherwise do. With

The problem is a nested loop over pairs costing O(n²) when the answer is one property of the sequence read once. Checking every pair of a sorted array for one summing to a target repeats comparisons a single sweep from both ends already rules out: once the current ends sum too high, every pair keeping that high end is too high too, so moving it on loses nothing.

the pointers keep true on every step, the thing you say out loud to justify the loop rather than trust it. For a sorted pair sum, it is that every pair before the low pointer or after the high one is already ruled out, so moving whichever end makes the sum too far from the target never skips the answer. For fast and slow, it is that everything before the slow pointer already holds the kept elements in order, the write-pointer idea used to compact an array in place. Either way each pointer moves at most n times, so the scan is O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
